All supplied changes are documentation only, with no source, config or workflow edits visible in these units. Nothing here weakens a control, so there is no qualifying finding.

prefix-cache.md (head lines 129-153) is a new section on the unregistered GLM sparse-state candidate. It documents a new full-state checkpoint layout, `native-paged-glm5next-full-state-v1`. It also states that SSD prefix-cache eligibility defaults on for `EigenLabs/GLM-5.3-Flash-MLX-NVFP4-mtp` via `PrefixCachePolicy.isGLM5NextDefaultModel`. `DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE=0` opts out, and GLM stays outside the registered coordinator serving models.

Relevant threat: T-041, the encrypted SSD tier, default-on with a per-donation gate, HMAC lookup tags and a 30-minute TTL. T-041 already says default-on covers every eligible CBv2 model. The new layout therefore appears to fall inside the accepted SEC-035 posture. T-041's affected_files do not list GLM or the new codec paths. I cannot verify from the supplied text that the new codec keeps the same HMAC naming, AAD, TTL and KEK controls, since the code is not in the diff.

model-registry.md (head 22-26) documents a raw GLM discovery quotation based on bounded headers and non-weight file sizes. It states there is no generic fallback for a malformed GLM inventory, and that only the shipped tokenizer is supported. It explicitly says this does not replace catalog/source identity or native validation. That is a restrictive, fail-closed statement.

inference.md (head 1207-1505) was reviewed as context only: MiMo audio/tool-schema/media decode accounting, Flash-Next admission, and GLM tool-suffix validation that fails closed. These are descriptions of existing behavior, with no new boundary claims beyond the existing ones. The doc keeps memory gates, caps and ownership checks mandatory.

A later pass with the code should confirm that the GLM full-state SSD store reuses the SSDLookupKeys/DBK3 AAD/TTL controls, and should consider adding GLM to T-041's affected_files.
